sections.h2: Where is Laramie, Wyoming, and what is the setting?
sections.html:
Laramie is the county seat of Albany County, in southeastern Wyoming, about 50 miles from Cheyenne and roughly 25 miles north of the Colorado line. It sits on the Laramie River at the point where Interstate 80 meets U.S. Route 287.

The city stands at about 7,165 feet on a high plain between two mountain ranges. That elevation shapes everything from heating bills to how long snow stays on a roof.

Denver is about 130 miles away, and the University of Wyoming describes Laramie as affordable compared with many college towns. Outdoor areas nearby include Vedauwoo, the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest and the Snowy Range Ski Area.

Laramie dates to 1868, when the Union Pacific Railroad platted the town and began selling lots on April 20. Track reached the town on May 4, 1868, and Laramie was officially incorporated on January 13, 1874.

The railroad chose Laramie for a major repair depot with machine shops, a roundhouse and a power plant. Population jumped past 3,000 during construction, then fell to about 800 once the crews left. An 1874 rolling mill that reprocessed iron rails eventually employed 300 men.

The University of Wyoming came out of an 1880s deal that gave Cheyenne the state capital and Laramie the university. It opened in September 1887 with 40 students. Downtown and the West Side are both listed as historic districts, and Laramie has 21 sites on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Ivinson Mansion and Old Main on campus.

The University of Wyoming is Laramie's largest employer, with nearly 3,000 employees, according to the Wyoming state history encyclopedia. The same source says tourism, health care and retail together provide about as many jobs as the university.

Railroad jobs began to decline in the mid-1950s, and the university took over as the anchor. Enrollment was about 8,200 students in live instruction in fall 2024, plus nearly 2,300 online, per Wikipedia. The median age in the 2020 census was 27.2, which is young for a Wyoming city.

For sellers, that mix matters in two ways:

  • A young population means many Laramie households rent, so some sellers are landlords rather than owner-occupants.
  • The university is one large employer, so changes there can matter to local housing demand.

sections.h2: What does Laramie's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Laramie has a cold semi-arid climate with long, dry winters and short, warm summers. Average temperature is about 21 degrees Fahrenheit in December and 64 in July. Annual precipitation runs about 10.5 to 11 inches, and annual snowfall is about 48 to 50 inches.

The growing season is short, with freezing temperatures possible from September 14 through June 6. Record extremes run from 96 degrees in July to minus 50.

The city's building office lists local design criteria such as snow loads, wind speeds, frost depth and seismic classification in its Bulletin #2. A buyer reviewing a Laramie house will likely ask about roof condition, insulation and furnace age.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and airport serve Laramie?
sections.html:
Albany County School District #1 is headquartered in Laramie and is the only district in the county. It operates 19 public schools, and the Laramie schools include seven elementary schools, one middle school, Laramie High School and Whiting High School. Snowy Range Academy is a K-7 charter school, and the UW Lab School covers K-9.

Interstate 80 and U.S. 287 meet in town. The business route of I-80 runs along Grand Avenue. Laramie Regional Airport is about three miles west of downtown on WYO 130, with SkyWest flying to Denver for United.

sections.h2: What permits and zoning rules affect a Laramie house sale?
sections.html:
Laramie requires a building permit for most residential projects and repairs. The city follows the 2024 International Building Code with local amendments in Laramie Municipal Code Chapter 15.24.

The Code Administration page lists work that does not need a permit:

  • One-story sheds and playhouses under 200 square feet that meet setbacks.
  • Fences up to 7 feet high in back and side yards only.
  • Retaining walls up to 4 feet high, measured from the bottom of the footing.
  • Unattached decks under 200 square feet that are no more than 30 inches above grade and do not serve the front door.
  • Painting, papering and similar finish work.

Permits are filed through the city's online Civic Access portal, and the estimated plan review period is three weeks. Code Administration is at 406 Ivinson Avenue, phone 307-721-5271.

Zoning comes from the Unified Development Code. The city lists many zoning districts and overlays, including the Aquifer Protection Overlay and the Gateway Overlay. Planning asks owners to reach out before buying property, changing a use or dividing land. The Planning Division is at 320 E Grand Avenue, (307) 721-5207, or planning@cityoflaramie.org.

If you have a converted basement, an old addition or an unpermitted deck, ask Code Administration what it would take to bring it into compliance before a buyer finds it.

sections.h2: When are Albany County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Wyoming law sets the property tax calendar for every county, including Albany County. The first half is due on or after September 1 and payable on or after November 10. The second half is due on or after March 1 and payable on or after May 10 of the following year. Paying the full amount by December 31 avoids interest and penalty.

Unpaid balances accrue interest at 18 percent per year. The statute text we read is a 2012 copy, so confirm the current terms with the county.

The Albany County Treasurer's number is 307-721-2502, and the Assessor's is 307-721-2511. The county has an online tax portal for looking up and paying bills. The county courthouse is at 525 E Grand Avenue.

Wyoming's Homeowner's Exemption removes 25 percent of taxable value on the first $1 million of fair market value for a primary residence. The Long-term Homeowner's Exemption removes 50 percent on the first $3 million for owners 65 or older with at least 25 years of Wyoming residential property tax payments. For tax year 2027, the owner must live in the home at least eight months of the year. The County Assessor reviews each application.

sections.h2: How is a Laramie sale recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds in Albany County are recorded with the County Clerk, which is Kayla White's office at 307-721-2541. Under Wyoming Statute 18-3-402, the clerk stamps each instrument with the day, hour and minute it arrives and keeps indexes of grantors and grantees.

The date of record is the filing date, and the clerk cannot record a document until the fee is paid. Before listing, you can pull your recorded deed, any easements and any recorded agreements so a buyer sees clean paperwork.

sections.h2: What do Laramie sellers usually face, and when does a cash sale help?
sections.html:
Laramie sellers often face rental houses with deferred maintenance, estates, job moves and houses needing roof or insulation work. A cash sale helps when you want to avoid repairs, showings and a financing contingency.

A cash offer from our team is based on the house as it is. We review condition, location and the work a buyer would take on, then make an offer you can accept or decline. We do not promise a price before seeing the property.

  • Traditional listing: more exposure and often a higher price, with commission, repairs and a longer timeline.
  • Cash sale: fewer steps and a faster close, typically at a lower price than a prepared listing.

Tell us early about back taxes, liens, tenants or a mortgage balance. Those details shape the closing steps and the paperwork the title company will need.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Laramie house as a rental with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Often yes, though lease terms and timing need to be reviewed. Tell us about the lease and the move-out date so we can plan the closing.

faqs.q: When are Albany County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and payable by November 10, and the second half is due March 1 and payable by May 10. Paying everything by December 31 avoids interest on the first half. Call the Albany County Treasurer at 307-721-2502 to confirm your balance.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for work on my Laramie house before selling?
faqs.a: Most residential projects and repairs need a building permit, with exceptions for small sheds, low fences, short retaining walls and finish work. Contact Laramie Code Administration at 307-721-5271 before starting. You do not need a permit to sell, but unpermitted work can complicate a sale.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Laramie property?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded with the Albany County Clerk, phone 307-721-2541. The clerk stamps the time of receipt and requires the fee up front.

faqs.q: Does winter affect selling a house in Laramie?
faqs.a: It can. Laramie averages about 48 to 50 inches of snow a year, and freezing temperatures are possible from mid-September through early June. Plan inspections and closings with winter weather in mind.
